gen-dafont-gobold-fs-quicksand: Gobold spreads its wide, commanding letters along the line, curves left stubbornly open and ascenders kept short. Quicksand's tall, rounded lowercase sits beneath in a friendly sans.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-abyssinica-sil: Loud, geometric, spaced out. Gobold stamps its short-ascendered capitals across the top, while Abyssinica SIL follows in a literary serif whose line weight shifts softly, like watercolor.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-cambo: Cambo is a refined, bookish serif, with a short step from lowercase to capital and a modest thick-thin rhythm. And Gobold brings the pipe-cleaner stoutness, wide-set and geometric, that Cambo never attempts.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-manuale: Commanding up top, Gobold draws its lines like smooth tubing. Manuale underneath has large-eyed lowercase, moderate contrast and crossbars slightly thinner than its stems, so a long passage reads in a traditional, editorial voice.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-naskh-arabic: Noto Naskh Arabic is a refined serif with very tall lowercase and modest contrast, like lightly engraved brass. And Gobold's strength is the opposite: no calligraphic thinning, just wide-spaced, commanding geometry.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-nastaliq-urdu: Thin steel rod seems bent into every Gobold letter, with open curves and short ascenders spread wide. Noto Nastaliq Urdu then tucks in below as a dignified serif with tight vertical rhythm and light modulation.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-rashi-hebrew: Gobold draws a constant-width line like a marker, wide-set and geometric, with short ascenders. Noto Rashi Hebrew takes over as a bookish serif, its crossbars slightly thinner than the stems.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-ahom: A monoline construction, with curves that never quite close, marks Gobold out at the top. Noto Serif Ahom lets a text serif with lofty lowercase take over below.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-armenian: Gobold sets stout, cable-like letters wide apart. Noto Serif Armenian below is a traditional serif with open counters and a gentle stem-to-hairline ratio, which softens the headline's commanding weight into something authoritative yet approachable.
gen-dafont-gobold-gf-noto-serif-balinese: Editorial in spirit, this pair puts Gobold's stout, wide-set geometry over Noto Serif Balinese, whose lowercase carries real vertical presence and in-between stroke contrast, so a long passage reads like a traditional classic serif page.
